summary:
Kalmykia is an autonomous republic of the Russian Federation and stands under the national framework. The national layer carries the ban on legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care, the propaganda statutes, the extremist designation of the LGBT movement, and the absence of anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection; those are recorded on the parent record and are not restated here.

Region-specific signal: no Kalmykia-specific enforcement incidents, local ordinances, or regional institutions governing trans people were identified in the source inventory. The assessment for a trans visitor to Kalmykia is therefore the national assessment.

One index reading covers Kalmykia directly: for 2024 to 2026, Russia including Kalmykia scored 2% on the European LGBTI legal and policy index, ranking joint-lowest alongside Azerbaijan. The index records explicit bans and legal limitations that make legal gender recognition practically impossible for trans people.
tangentialFactors:
The national propaganda provisions and the November 2023 Supreme Court extremist designation apply in Kalmykia as everywhere in Russia, exposing a trans visitor to arrest, fines and prosecution for visible identity expression, association or advocacy. Kalmykia contributes no separate regional record of such enforcement.

The 2% index score is a national figure that includes Kalmykia; it is not a Kalmykia-specific measurement and does not distinguish the republic from other Russian regions.
localsOnly: Residents of Kalmykia are subject to the national prohibitions on legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care, with no regional alternative route. No regional anti-discrimination protection, hate-crime designation, or local registration practice specific to Kalmykia was identified in the inventory.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Kalmykia-specific data on local police practice, regional courts, healthcare facilities, or documented violence against trans people was present in the source inventory; the absence of such records is not evidence that none exists.

The inventory's detailed national material on extremist-designation prosecutions, pride-permit litigation, and hate-crime counts belongs to the parent record and is not verified here as region-specific.
